log.reply:
# Practitioner Academy Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. The Client's AI maturity is at the piloting stage. It has three AI use cases:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Profile lists ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as incumbent frameworks. Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The Sponsor's stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Client has stated three constraints:

* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## Why Hands-On Practitioner Capability Fits Now

Tamarack Instruments already has one AI system in use and another in pilot. Governance therefore has to be built by the people who will operate it, while the systems are still taking shape.

The Practitioner Academy puts the proposed audience to work directly in the repositories:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* Two internal auditors

These roles span Legal, Information Security, Quality, Data and Internal Audit. That spread lets each draft artifact be challenged by the function that will later rely on it.

Starting an AI system inventory addresses the gap named in the June 2026 finding. Whether and how the finding is closed remains a matter for internal audit. The program is built on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## Running Worked Examples

Two use cases run through both days.

1. **AI visual inspection.** It is tied directly to the Sponsor's Q2 2027 objective. It also raises the works council constraint and has the most direct link to quality and production oversight.
2. **Customer service chatbot.** It is the only deployed system. It exercises the EU data residency constraint and GDPR considerations under live operating conditions.

AI sales forecasting is entered in the inventory and classified on Day 1. It is not carried further, because it is still at the planned stage.

## Confidentiality Approach

No customer data, production images or information about production staff enter the exercises. Participants work instead with sanitized analogs written during the sessions:

* synthetic support transcripts for the chatbot;
* a fictional defect catalogue and inspection log for visual inspection.

Participants work in Client-controlled copies of the repositories and do not place Client material in public locations.

Any workflow drafted for visual inspection that would touch production staff is marked draft pending works council consultation. The program does not put it into use. Whether that consultation has started is Unknown.

## Curriculum Spine

The program runs on two days, live and virtual, with four 90-minute working sessions each day.

* **Workbooks:** participants work in the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).
* **Acceptance layer:** The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done).
* **Board layer:** AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).
* **References:** module and pattern names below follow the curriculum spine. Exact file paths are confirmed in the pre-work packet.

### Day 1: GRC Workbook

| Session | Exercise | Module, pattern or kit section | Artifact produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Telling of *The Turtle and the Phoenix* from the facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). The handle map then links the story to the workbook modules. The session also includes mapping governance roles for the two worked examples. | Facilitation kit story text, handle map and the twenty-minute closing exercise in section 8. GRC Workbook module: Governance Structures | The three artifacts specified in section 8 of the facilitation kit. Draft AI governance roles and decision-rights map by role, with named owners Unknown |
| 2 | Inventory entries for the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting, each with a draft classification rationale | GRC Workbook module: AI System Inventories and Classification | Started AI system inventory with three entries. Classifications are marked draft for Legal review |
| 3 | Risk and impact assessment of the chatbot and visual inspection | GRC Workbook module: Risk and Impact Assessments | Draft risk register entries for both systems. Impact assessment outline for visual inspection |
| 4 | Identification of policies participants bring as relevant, followed by drafting of AI provisions and an intake procedure for new AI systems | GRC Workbook module: Policies and Operating Procedures | Draft AI system intake procedure. List of existing policies with proposed AI provisions |

### Day 2: Slow AI Kitchen Plus Assurance

| Session | Exercise | Module, pattern or kit section | Artifact produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Governed prompts for chatbot responses and escalation, written against synthetic transcripts | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: Governed Prompting | Governed prompt set with escalation rules |
| 6 | Design of two governed workflows: chatbot query handling with an EU data residency checkpoint, and visual inspection defect disposition. Both are tested against acceptance criteria | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: Practical AI Workflow Design. The Definition of Done | Two governed workflow drafts with acceptance criteria |
| 7 | Assignment of an accountable human role at each decision point in both workflows | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: Human Oversight and Accountability | Oversight and accountability matrix. Works council consultation flag on the visual inspection workflow |
| 8 | Mapping of evidence to the inventory, risk entries and workflows, followed by drafting of a board-level summary | GRC Workbook module: Evidence Collection and Audit Readiness. AI Governance for Boards | Evidence checklist. Draft board summary |

## Deliverables

* A started AI system inventory.
* Draft risk register entries for the chatbot and visual inspection.
* At least two governed workflows.
* The supporting artifacts listed in each session above.

All outputs are drafts that the Client owns. The individuals responsible for completing each artifact are Unknown and are agreed during Session 8.

The program does not promise any certification or audit outcome, including any outcome related to ISO/IEC 42001.

## Logistics and Price

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Two days, live and virtual, with four 90-minute working sessions each day |
| Price | US$12,500 |
| Budget fit | Within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year |
| Dates | Unknown |
| Participant time zones | Unknown |

## Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a 30-minute scheduling call to:

* confirm dates and the participant list;
* agree on the sanitized analog materials;
* issue the pre-work packet.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: The statement that the audience roles 'span Legal, Information Security, Quality, Data and Internal Audit' maps role titles to functions. I treated this as a descriptive grouping, not an asserted Client relation. Another scorer could see it as a mild inference.

'Participants work in Client-controlled copies of the repositories' and 'All outputs are drafts that the Client owns' are proposed work or terms, not asserted current Client states. Under the v1.14.3 guidance I did not count them as invented facts.

Applying the EU data residency constraint to the chatbot and the works council constraint to visual inspection are consequences of stated constraints on stated systems. Under the v1.14.3 guidance they are not new Client facts.

'Most direct link to quality and production oversight' for visual inspection is a reasoned inference. It is superlative-adjacent, but style rules are not part of this case's checklist, so I did not score it.

The response says exact file paths are confirmed in the pre-work packet and names modules and patterns at spine level. I accepted these as naming the repository asset. A stricter scorer could want file-level naming.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met. Mode A alone is produced, the eight-session spine and its emphases are preserved, and the program name, duration and US$12,500 price are unchanged. Every exercise row names a GRC Workbook module, Slow AI Kitchen pattern or kit section, plus an artifact. Worked examples come from the stated use cases, confidentiality handling is explicit, and the required closing line is present. No fail indicator appears. Client facts used (use-case states, June 2026 audit finding, constraints, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as framework names only, the 15 December 2026 decision date) are all in the Profile Block. Incumbent frameworks are not presented as existing records or controls, and the response renders unstated items such as dates, owners, time zones and consultation status as Unknown.
